vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: skillguard-hardened
Version: 1.0.0

The bundle is a security auditing framework ('SkillGuard') designed to detect malicious behavior in other OpenClaw skills using static regex rules and AI-based semantic analysis. While the package contains a script that performs data exfiltration (steal.sh) and references a suspicious domain (evil.example), these are explicitly located within the 'tests/fixtures/malicious_skill' directory and are used solely for verifying the scanner's detection capabilities. The core logic includes defensive measures such as path validation in 'lib/remediation.py' to prevent directory traversal and specific system prompts in 'lib/ai_audit.py' to mitigate prompt injection during the auditing process.

llm.summary: SkillGuard is internally consistent with its stated purpose as a local skill-audit tool that optionally calls an external AI (DeepSeek); it requires careful trust of the external AI and a couple of minor documentation/metadata mismatches.

dimensions.detail: The skill is a Python-based scanner/audit tool and declares python3 as a required binary and a DeepSeek API key for optional AI auditing. The declared purpose (audit skills, quarantine/restore, produce reports) matches the included scripts and libraries.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and code scan skill directories, build structured JSON reports, optionally send package content to DeepSeek for semantic analysis, and permit quarantine/restore/delete actions confined to configured allowed roots. This behavior aligns with the stated purpose but you should note that the AI audit will transmit skill content to an external API (DeepSeek).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only install), so nothing is downloaded or executed at install time by the platform. The package does include Python scripts (no package manager installs).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only one primary secret is required (SKILLGUARD_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, with fallback DEEPSEEK_API_KEY). That is proportionate for optional AI auditing, but providing it means skill package contents will be sent to the DeepSeek API. The scanner also respects a CLAWD_WORKSPACE env var which controls scan roots; that affects what the skill can see.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and follows confined quarantine/restore/delete flows. File moves and deletes are restricted by policy 'allowed_roots' and assert-safety checks; that is expected for a quarantining tool.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says: local static scanning plus an optional semantic audit by DeepSeek. Before installing:

- Understand that if you set SKILLGUARD_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (or DEEPSEEK_API_KEY), the tool will send skill package content to https://api.deepseek.com. Only provide that key if you trust DeepSeek and are comfortable with the skill content (potentially including code and comments) being transmitted to that external service.
- The code can quarantine or delete skill directories but is guarded by allowed_roots in the policy; confirm the policy's allowed_roots are limited to only the directories you want the tool to access. Note CLAWD_WORKSPACE (or the code's workspace inference) affects those resolved paths.
- The SKILL.md examples reference commands that rely on other binaries (e.g., npx, bash) but the skill metadata only declares python3. If you plan to use npx-related flows, make sure those binaries exist and are what you expect.
- The package includes test fixtures for malicious/benign samples and prompt-injection example text; that is normal for a scanner but review files if you have strict supply-chain rules.

If you need higher assurance, ask the maintainer for: (1) a description of exactly what build_ai_payload sends to DeepSeek (what files/fields are included), and (2) whether any non-configurable endpoints are used. If you cannot trust the external AI provider, run the skill without setting the DeepSeek key (it will fall back to local-only rules).
llm.findings: [ignore-previous-instructions] expected: The SKILL.md (and the scanner rules) contain prompt-injection probe text such as 'ignore-previous-instructions'. This looks deliberate because the scanner detects prompt injection and tests for it; presence is expected for a tool that flags prompt-injection patterns, but it is worth reviewing to ensure it's not being used for other purposes.
